subject.title: feat(gateway): add context engine control API

question: Should context-engine control ship as an HTTP-only operator API, as normal Gateway RPC methods, or be deferred until the plugin API/security contract is designed?
rationale: The branch adds both public ContextEngine methods and advertised Gateway method names, so the correct permanent API boundary is a maintainer product/API decision rather than a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Document HTTP-only API
options.body: Keep the HTTP routes, remove the misleading core Gateway method descriptors, and document auth scopes, request payloads, and sanitized result contracts.

options.title: Add Gateway RPC API
options.body: Keep the advertised contextEngine.* names only if the PR adds real Gateway RPC handlers, protocol docs, and tests for those methods.

options.title: Defer the control surface
options.body: Pause or close this branch until maintainers explicitly sponsor the context-engine control API and security model.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP-only API
recommendation.body: Keep the HTTP routes, remove the misleading core Gateway method descriptors, and document auth scopes, request payloads, and sanitized result contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent plugin SDK/context-engine capability work makes them the strongest available owner for the API-boundary choice.
